lesson_flow: Start with a direct child-friendly definition of the topic.
Explain the main features, parts, or types of the topic.
State why the topic is important in daily life.
Use at least two specific real-life examples a child can picture.
End with a short recap and understanding questions.
explanation_requirements: Do not explain how a teacher should teach the lesson.
Do not give meta-instructions such as 'Begin by telling the learner'.
Write the actual lesson note the student should read.
Use specific examples instead of placeholders or generic phrases.

must_cover: clear meaning or definition
main properties, characteristics, or parts
importance to life, health, or the environment
everyday examples from home, school, weather, plants, animals, or the body
resource_search_terms: labelled science diagram for primary school

air.hook: Learners already feel air when the wind blows, when they fan themselves, or when they blow up a balloon.
must_cover: air is all around us even though we cannot see it
air occupies space
moving air is called wind
people, animals, and plants need air to live
simple examples such as balloons, tyres, kites, breathing, and wind
worked_examples: Explain how a balloon becomes bigger when it is filled with air.
Explain how we know air is present when tree leaves move or a kite flies.
real_world_examples: breathing in the classroom or at home
a bicycle tyre filled with air
a balloon used during a birthday celebration
misconceptions: air is not nothing; it is a real substance around us
because we cannot see air does not mean it is absent

must_cover: meaning of the grammar idea in simple words
clear examples in sentences
why the concept helps speaking, reading, and writing
common mistakes children make

parts of speech.hook: Every word in a sentence has a job to do.
must_cover: meaning of parts of speech
the eight parts of speech in simple language
at least one sentence example for each major part
why knowing parts of speech helps writing and speaking
worked_examples: Identify noun and verb in a simple sentence.
Show the difference between an adjective and an adverb using one sentence.
misconceptions: the same word can do different jobs in different sentences
small words like prepositions and conjunctions are still important

must_cover: what the concept means
when to use it
step-by-step worked solutions
common mistakes and how to avoid them
